newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes U.N. rights win, hopes for talks.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes U.N. rights win, hopes for talks.

text.p: Beijing rejoiced on Wednesday at its sinking of a resolution in the United Nations to fault its human rights record and urged the West to draw a lesson from its seventh straight failure to censure China.

"The Chinese government hereby expresses its admiration and gratitude to all the countries that have upheld jusice and rendered support to China," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said in a statement.
China rallied strong support from Third World countries at the United Nations Human Rights Commission in Geneva, sinking a Western resolution criticising its rights record and treatment of Tibet.
"China is heartened to note that a considerable number of Western countries have stayed away from co-sponsoring this year's anti-China draft resolution," Shen said.

"We hope the United States, Denmark and a few other countries that have clung to a confrontational approach will...draw a lesson from their failure and make a clear break from their erroneous practice of tabling an anti-China draft resolution," he said.
